ai.description: The Wadi Racer reaches 100–130 cm. It is slender, typically grey or olive with a distinct reddish or orange vertebral stripe and large, prominent eyes. It features smooth scales and a fast, agile gait.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Platyceps rhodorachis* is the presence of a distinct, thin reddish or pinkish vertebral stripe running along the length of its back.
ai.habitat: The Wadi Racer inhabits arid, rocky hillsides and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically ranging from sea level up to 2,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Wadi Racer is a highly agile, diurnal snake that uses its exceptional speed to actively forage for lizards and small rodents across rocky desert terrain.
ai.reproductionNotes: Platyceps rhodorachis is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–12 eggs. Breeding occurs during the spring and summer months.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Wadi Racer occurs across arid regions of northwestern India, including Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Punjab, typically inhabiting plains and hills up to 2,000 meters.
